summary: The note defines Opening Day as the day professional baseball leagues begin their regular season, typically in the first week of April for Major League Baseball and most minor leagues. It then describes how MLB shifted its opening days in 2011, 2012 and 2018, with schedule changes driven partly by the goal of keeping the World Series out of November. The 2018 season opened with all 30 teams on the same day, a first since 1968.
one_line: Opening Day is the day professional baseball leagues begin their regular season, usually in early April, and MLB's opening dates shifted in 2011, 2012 and 2018.
key_facts: Opening Day is the day on which professional baseball leagues begin their regular season.
For Major League Baseball and most minor leagues, Opening Day typically falls during the first week of April.
Major League Baseball had most of its teams open the 2011 season on a Thursday (March 31) or Friday (April 1) rather than the traditional Monday.
MLB opened the 2011 season on Thursday or Friday in order to prevent the World Series from extending into November.
Most MLB teams opened the 2012 season on Thursday (April 5) or Friday (April 6).
Subsequent MLB seasons through 2017 returned to Monday openers for most teams.
For the 2018 season, all 30 MLB teams were scheduled to open on Thursday, March 29.
The March 29, 2018 start was the earliest domestic start for a regular season in MLB history.
2018 was the first time since 1968 that all major league teams were scheduled to start the season on the same day.
Two games on the 2018 opening day were subsequently rained out and postponed to Friday, March 30.
